# OpenCode Zen FreeX Use **OpenCode Zen's free models** in [magpie](https://github.com/yetone/magpie) Shared `public` credential · Automatic discovery · Native streaming protocols [简体中文](https://github.com/tkhs101/OpenCode-Zen-FreeX/blob/main/README.md) · **English** Machine-readable docs: [llms.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tkhs101/OpenCode-Zen-FreeX/main/llms.txt) · [llms-full.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tkhs101/OpenCode-Zen-FreeX/main/llms-full.txt) (generated by `bun run docs:llms` from this README and MAINTAINING.md) [![CI](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/tkhs101/OpenCode-Zen-FreeX/ci.yml?branch=main&style=flat-square&label=CI)](https://github.com/tkhs101/OpenCode-Zen-FreeX/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/opencode-zen-freex?style=flat-square&logo=npm&logoColor=white)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/opencode-zen-freex) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green.svg?style=flat-square)](LICENSE) [![Runtime: bun](https://img.shields.io/badge/runtime-bun-f472b6?style=flat-square&logo=bun&logoColor=white)](https://bun.sh)
## Why this fork [zen-free](https://github.com/magpie-community/plugins/tree/main/packages/zen-free) is this plugin's predecessor. Let's be clear: upstream is maintained, and bugs are fixed quickly. The problem is that it has never had a **stable, explicit position** on **free-model support**. When a free model stops working, the issue gets the answer that it **will no longer be supported**; some time later the same problem is quietly fixed and the free model works again. Support, drop, support again — users are left churning with upstream's position, never able to tell **how long the support will last**. If people depend on it, it deserves a clear answer rather than **more flip-flopping** — that is why this project exists. | UTC | Commit | What upstream said | | --- | --- | --- | | 2026-10-13 23:53 | [`643ef50`](https://github.com/magpie-community/plugins/commit/643ef5018e63be78c4aa7554696831d4220ac9c9) | The README adds a note that the free tier only works inside OpenCode itself, `this plugin doesn't work around that`; use a paid Zen key or OpenCode Go instead. The commit message says `No version bump … The code on main is left as it is` | | 2026-10-14 10:57 | [`a810ee7`](https://github.com/magpie-community/plugins/commit/a810ee7e882012ab106e2deb742176cd43db781a) | 0.1.6 **deletes** that note and sends OpenCode 1.19.0's own headers — 11 hours after it was added | | 2026-10-14 17:59 | [`5fc0a75`](https://github.com/magpie-community/plugins/commit/5fc0a75292f0e5c0c10cf65a188bff5545d6b8e9) | 0.1.7: `free models answer again` | Later upstream changes are merged as needed, while this branch keeps its own choices (for example, the system prompt and complete tool set are captured per generation from a real OpenCode rather than pinned to one version). ## Installation and login ```sh magpie plugin add opencode-zen-freex magpie plugin login opencode-zen-free ``` Use `public` as the key. It is the free tier's shared credential; no personal API key is needed — anything else you enter is discarded. Personal keys belong in magpie's built-in OpenCode Zen provider: it accepts several keys and switches or fails over between them. Credentials live in OpenCode's `auth.json` or magpie's `plugin-auth.json`. ## Models Model names are written `opencode-zen-free/`, for example `opencode-zen-free/big-pickle`. - **Automatic discovery**: when the host lists models, the plugin reads Zen's list; repeated listings within 60 seconds reuse the previous result. A successful read is cached (`~/.cache/opencode-zen-freex/discovery.json`, `%LOCALAPPDATA%` on Windows); when the list cannot be read, the plugin falls back to the cache or the table shipped in the package, and when the cache is used, its age is passed to the host. The protocol table has its own snapshot (`models-observed.json`, published hourly by a repository workflow that diffs OpenCode's docs page, fetched in the background): when the docs cannot be read, or an id's endpoint row was withdrawn, the snapshot or the bundled copy answers, and no model is asked at the wrong endpoint. - **Limits are measured**: the catalogue, vendor claims and the wall the route actually enforces often disagree. Context is declared at the largest value measured to pass; output prefers the paid twin's declaration on the same gateway. For example, `mimo-v2.6-flash-free`'s catalogue says 200k, but 375k was served; `glm-5.3-flash-free`'s paid twin claims 1M, but 323k was the largest that passed; and the route's own refusals count too — `deepseek-v4.1-flash-free` fell from 1M to 326k after it began refusing above roughly 326,700 tokens. See [`MAINTAINING.md`'s “Limits Zen under-reports”](MAINTAINING.md#limits-zen-under-reports) for the measurements and how to re-run them. - **Limits are also learned from traffic**: the plugin sends no extra requests; it only probes upward and converges downward with requests it is already forwarding. Learned values survive restarts, and a refused model is pulled back to a size already proven to pass. - **Measured snapshots without waiting for a release**: the repository runs an incremental sweep every hour, writes `limits-observed.json` and publishes it on `main`; after startup the plugin fetches it in the background at most once per hour, falling back to its cache or the copy in the package. - **The list is authoritative**: `-free` models on Zen's list are offered immediately (except on protocols this plugin does not support), without waiting for the catalogue; a catalogue that cannot be read only affects what it describes, and does not make the list a fallback. - **No longer free means 404**: the error lists the models that are free at that moment; once a model is free again, refresh the list. Availability and rate limits belong to Zen; the plugin cannot see remaining quota. ## Requests Requests go to `https://opencode.ai/inference/v1` in each model's native protocol (Chat Completions / Responses / Anthropic Messages); both streaming and plain JSON are supported. - **Borrow only OpenCode's shell**: headers, User-Agent, the system prompt and the complete tool set are matched to the current 2.x generation of OpenCode (the 1.x lane was retired by the free tier on 2026-10-25; a retired lane is not something any wording recovers). The official prompt goes in front of the host's own system instructions; a body that already carries it is left alone, so repeated shaping cannot duplicate it. The prompt ends at OpenCode's environment block — no built-in skill is advertised, because a host that is not OpenCode has none of them to load. The requests also have to **leave from a Bun runtime**, as the official clients do: magpie runs its plugins under the Bun it ships, which is what this package rides. The header set is deliberately minimal — **do not add your own**; two individually harmless headers can be refused together. - **The host's tools still run**: each one keeps its own wording and parameters but travels under a `clint_` name, so it cannot collide with the official set that follows it. Every tool reference in the request is renamed with it, and names in the reply are translated back; the host never sees a name it did not declare. OpenCode's own tools are sent in their complete, captured form — and because the official prompt teaches Code Mode, the prompt is followed by a `` naming the `clint_` tools this host actually runs, so the model does not open the session by calling `execute` to an unknown-tool error. - **Unknown tool names go to the host as written**: match exactly first, then case-insensitively, then ignoring `_`/`-`/`.`/whitespace, and accept only a unique result; when nothing matches or the match is ambiguous, the call is neither guessed nor dropped — the model's name, id and arguments reach the host as written, which replies with its own "no such tool"; the model then renames the call and retries. Only calls with no name at all are omitted, and the body says so. - **One identity is held for a window, one per conversation**: an OpenCode-shaped session id and a project id are minted together, held for 60 seconds by default, and replaced together when the window ends — the timestamp is the current moment, always inside the window the tier accepts. The window is per conversation, not per process: a different name from the host (the CLI sends `x-opencode-session` on every request) is a different pair, so two conversations running at once each hold their own, and a refusal rotates only the conversation it refused. A request that names nothing shares one slot — requests nothing can tell apart are requests the tier cannot tell apart either. Bursts of fresh identities are refused where the same requests spaced about half a second apart pass (measured). `OPENCODE_ZEN_FREE_IDENTITY_TTL_MS=0` mints a fresh pair per request instead, which is also what measuring one ledger needs. Set `OPENCODE_ZEN_FREE_SESSION_AFFINITY=1` for one session per conversation kept indefinitely (an OpenCode-shaped id from the host passed through; otherwise one derived from the host's session identifiers and remembered, so every turn shares an id), where the window is not consulted. - **The project id is its own too**: the shared `public` credential identifies no one, so quota has nothing to do with the key — it is ledgered along the dimensions that do distinguish traffic: an egress-IP budget, and per-(project id × egress) ledgers beneath it. While the egress has room, a fresh id on a spent exit is a new ledger (measured 2026-10-26); on a popular exit the egress budget is spent by everyone routed through the same IP, and no fresh id opens anything: a ~32k-token request refused five times, then a ~5k one five more, and two such rounds after those — twenty fresh ids, one answer: 429 (measured 2026-10-27 on a US exit whose admission probe had just passed — our own spend there in the minutes in between was ~10k tokens, so the exhaustion was the world's, not ours). On a saturated exit, waiting is what helps. A host that names its project keeps that name across windows; one that does not gets a random git-hash-shaped id held for the window above — the old `global` default was one bucket shared by every freeriding plugin user on the planet, pre-burned on popular exits. - **Truncation and errors are reported honestly**: if a stream ends early, a Chat stream with content and no unfinished tool call is completed as a normal answer marked truncated; anything else fails. The error body is read only far enough to find a limit Zen itself states; the rest is replaced with an explanation.
Full rules for headers and session ids **Headers** are exactly: `content-type`, `accept`, `user-agent`, `x-opencode-project`, `x-opencode-session` and `x-opencode-session-id` (the same value), `x-opencode-client: cli`, `authorization: Bearer public`; Messages uses `x-api-key: public` plus `anthropic-version` instead. The plugin never sets `anthropic-beta` itself — it passes it through only when the host sends it. **Session id**: the default holds one session for the window and reads none of what follows; `OPENCODE_ZEN_FREE_IDENTITY_TTL_MS=0` gives a fresh one per request. With `OPENCODE_ZEN_FREE_SESSION_AFFINITY=1`, the conversation is named in order from the session headers `x-opencode-session` / `x-opencode-session-id` / `x-session-affinity` / `x-session-id` / `session_id` / `conversation-id` / `conversation_id`, then the body's `conversation_id`, `metadata.session_id`, or the `_session_` inside Claude Code's `metadata.user_id`. If none of those exists, the system/instructions and the first user message form the seed (a changed system prompt is a different conversation); only after that is `previous_response_id` consulted, and failing that a new id is generated every time. An empty string is never a name.
## When the free tier stops answering The 403 this plugin returns names the OpenCode version its prompt and tool definitions were captured from; start there. All three commands **run only in a repository checkout** (`check:gate` and `capture` are not in the published package) and need Bun; `capture` also needs `opencode` on PATH: ```sh bun run check:gate # which fingerprints Zen accepts; 0 if a floor answers bun run capture -- --dry # all floors refused: capture, report the diff, write nothing bun run capture # write only after confirming the diff ``` `capture` rewrites `fingerprint.json` rather than refusing when the file is missing or broken. It does not write the prompt or the complete tool set: those live in `opencode-prompt-v1.txt` and `official-tools.json`, and a release updates them from the same OpenCode version as the capture (see [`MAINTAINING.md`](MAINTAINING.md#the-loop)). The gate is not stable: a verdict describes this moment only, so run it again before trusting it; repeated refusals from one address can also trigger a cooldown. For per-generation verdicts and how to read a failure, see [`MAINTAINING.md`'s “The loop”](MAINTAINING.md#the-loop) and [“Reading a failure”](MAINTAINING.md#reading-a-failure). ## Troubleshooting | Symptom | What to do | | --- | --- | | Every request is `403 FreeTierError`, with no egress-block wording | The captured OpenCode shape is stale. Update the plugin; from a repository checkout run `bun run check:gate`, and if every floor is refused, recapture the profile and refresh the prompt/tool assets from the same release | | The `403` body is a block notice (`abuse of traffic`, or `free models aren't available … from your current network`) | The free tier is blocking the current egress. Wait for the block to lift; retrying or rewriting the request will not help | | `426 Upgrade Required` | The package claims an older OpenCode version than Zen wants. Update the plugin, or run inside a newer OpenCode | | `404 … not available as an OpenCode Zen free model now` | Zen no longer offers this model for free. Pick another from the models listed in the error | | `Model is not an available free model for this protocol` | The list changed after the request was sent. Refresh the host's model list and retry | | `uses the public credential` | The stored key is not `public`. Log in again with `public` | | A `403` without `FreeTierError` | It is Zen's own 403, not this plugin's; read it as sent | | `400 context_length_exceeded`, or `max_tokens` out of range | The route enforces the model's own limits. Compact the conversation or lower `max_tokens`; context refusals state no window, while `max_tokens` refusals do state the allowed range | | The window looks too small and you want it re-learned, or a new environment variable has no effect | Delete `opencode-zen-freex/limits.json` under the cache directory (see Environment variables for where); environment variables are read only when the host starts, so restart it | | A model is asked for the wrong protocol | The endpoint table in the protocol docs could not be read. Set `OPENCODE_ZEN_FREE_MODELS_DEBUG=1` to see which document failed and why | | You want to check snapshot freshness or whether a model was retired | From a repository checkout run `bun limits-watch.mjs --status`; exit 0 is healthy, 2 is read but has issues, 1 is unreadable. `unavailable` is history only, not a disable switch | | The window stays at an old value, or `raw.githubusercontent.com` is unreachable | The remote snapshot is only an optimisation; a failure does not affect requests. Point it elsewhere or turn it off with the environment variables (see Environment variables) | ## Environment variables Common ones only; the full list and defaults are in [`.env.example`](https://github.com/tkhs101/OpenCode-Zen-FreeX/blob/main/.env.example). The cache directory is `%LOCALAPPDATA%` on Windows, and `$XDG_CACHE_HOME` or `~/.cache` elsewhere. | Variable | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `OPENCODE_ZEN_FREE_DISCOVERY_CACHE` | Discovery cache path; an empty string keeps discovery in memory only | | `OPENCODE_ZEN_FREE_SESSION_AFFINITY` | `1` keeps one session per conversation instead of the identity window | | `OPENCODE_ZEN_FREE_IDENTITY_TTL_MS` | Milliseconds one session and project id are held before both are replaced; default `60000` (60 seconds); `0` mints a fresh pair per request; capped at `86400000` | | `OPENCODE_ZEN_FREE_RETRY_429` | 429 retry count, default `2`; `0` turns the retry off | | `OPENCODE_ZEN_FREE_RETRY_WAIT_MS` | Milliseconds before the first retry, default `1200`, doubling per attempt | | `OPENCODE_ZEN_FREE_RETRY_WAIT_MAX_MS` | Wait ceiling, default `5000`; deliberately short by default — deployments that need longer set their own | | `OPENCODE_ZEN_FREE_RETRY_AFTER` | `1` honours a 429's own `retry-after` window (replaces one attempt's wait, still capped at 120 s); ignored by default | | `OPENCODE_ZEN_FREE_PACING_MS` | Smallest gap in milliseconds between two requests this loader sends; default `0` (off), capped at `30000` | | `OPENCODE_ZEN_FREE_MODELS_SNAPSHOT` | Bundled protocol-snapshot path; an empty string disables the bundled copy | | `OPENCODE_ZEN_FREE_MODELS_SNAPSHOT_URL` | Remote protocol-snapshot URL; an empty string disables the remote | | `OPENCODE_ZEN_FREE_MODELS_SNAPSHOT_CACHE` | Remote protocol-snapshot cache path; an empty string keeps it in memory only | | `OPENCODE_ZEN_FREE_MODELS_SNAPSHOT_REFRESH_MS` | Remote protocol-snapshot refresh interval, default `3600000` | | `OPENCODE_ZEN_FREE_MODELS_SNAPSHOT_TIMEOUT_MS` | Remote protocol-snapshot fetch timeout, default `5000` | | `OPENCODE_ZEN_FREE_LIMITS_SNAPSHOT` | Measured-snapshot path; an empty string disables reading a snapshot | | `OPENCODE_ZEN_FREE_LIMITS_SNAPSHOT_URL` | Remote snapshot URL; an empty string disables the remote | | `OPENCODE_ZEN_FREE_LIMITS_STATE` | Path to the learned-limit state; an empty string keeps it in memory only | | `OPENCODE_ZEN_FREE_LIMITS_DEBUG` | Set to `1` to log every raise, refusal, and route-stated window to stderr | | `OPENCODE_ZEN_FREE_MODELS_DEBUG` | Set to `1` to print catalogue-parsing details | | `OPENCODE_ZEN_FREE_MAX_WINDOW` | Upper bound for upward probing; ## 为什么有这个分支 [zen-free](https://github.com/magpie-community/plugins/tree/main/packages/zen-free) 是这个插件的前身。先说清楚：上游一直在维护，修 Bug 也很快。问题在于它对**免费模型支持**这件事，始终缺少一个**稳定、明确的态度** 免费模型失效时，用户反馈issue，得到的答复却是**将不再支持**；过一段时间，相关问题又被悄悄修复，免费模型重新恢复可用。支持、放弃、再支持——用户只能跟着上游的态度**反复折腾**，却始终无法确定这份支持究竟能持续多久 既然有人依赖它，就值得一个明确的答案，而不是**反复摇摆**，这就是本项目诞生的原因 | UTC | 提交 | 上游说了什么 | | --- | --- | --- | | 2026-10-13 23:53 | [`643ef50`](https://github.com/magpie-community/plugins/commit/643ef5018e63be78c4aa7554696831d4220ac9c9) | README 加上说明：免费层「只在 OpenCode 本体里能用」，`this plugin doesn't work around that`，请改用 Zen 付费 key 或 OpenCode Go；提交说明里写着 `No version bump … The code on main is left as it is` | | 2026-10-14 10:57 | [`a810ee7`](https://github.com/magpie-community/plugins/commit/a810ee7e882012ab106e2deb742176cd43db781a) | 0.1.6 把那段说明**删掉**，改为发 OpenCode 1.19.0 原样的请求头——距加上去 11 小时 | | 2026-10-14 17:59 | [`5fc0a75`](https://github.com/magpie-community/plugins/commit/5fc0a75292f0e5c0c10cf65a188bff5545d6b8e9) | 0.1.7：`free models answer again` | 上游的后续更新会按需合并，同时保留自己的取舍（比如系统提示词与完整工具集合按代从真实 OpenCode 采集，而不是钉死某一个版本） ## 安装与登录 ```sh magpie plugin add opencode-zen-freex magpie plugin login opencode-zen-free ``` 密钥填 `public`。这是 Zen 免费层的共享凭据，不需要个人 API key——填别的也会被丢掉。 个人 key 请加到 magpie 内置的 OpenCode Zen provider，那里支持多把 key 的切换与故障转移。凭据保存在 OpenCode 的 `auth.json` 或 magpie 的 `plugin-auth.json`。 ## 模型 模型名写作 `opencode-zen-free/`，例如 `opencode-zen-free/big-pickle`。 - **自动发现**：宿主列举模型时读取 Zen 的列表，60 秒内的重复列举复用上一次结果。读到的列表会写进缓存（`~/.cache/opencode-zen-freex/discovery.json`，Windows 在 `%LOCALAPPDATA%` 下）；列表读不到时由缓存或包内旧表顶替，有缓存时把数据的年龄一并告知宿主。协议端点表另有自己的快照（`models-observed.json`，仓库工作流每小时对照文档页增量发布，插件后台拉取）：文档页读不到或某模型的端点行被撤下时，由快照或包内副本顶替，模型不会被问到错误的端点上。 - **上限按实测**：目录、厂商自述与路由实际执行的墙常有出入。上下文按实测能过的最大值对齐，输出优先取同一网关付费孪生的声明。例如 `mimo-v2.6-flash-free` 目录写 20 万，实测 37.5 万；`glm-5.3-flash-free` 的付费孪生声明 100 万，实测 32.3 万；路由自己否掉的上限也照认，`deepseek-v4.1-flash-free` 的 100 万因此收紧到 32.6 万。依据与复测方法见 [`MAINTAINING.md` 的 “Limits Zen under-reports”](MAINTAINING.md#limits-zen-under-reports)。 - **上限还会从流量里学**：插件不额外发请求，只用自己转发的请求向上试探、向下收敛；学到的值重启后仍在，被拒的模型会自动收回到已经证明能过的尺寸。 - **实测快照不用等发版**：仓库每小时做一次增量实测，写入 `limits-observed.json` 并发布到 `main`；插件启动后每小时最多后台拉取一次，读不到就用缓存或包内副本。 - **列表说了算**：Zen 列表里的 `-free` 模型立即提供（本插件不支持的协议除外），不等目录补齐；目录读不到只影响它描述的那部分，不代表列表是回退结果。 - **不再免费即 404**：错误会列出当时可用的免费模型；模型重新免费后，刷新列表即可。可用性与限流归 Zen 管，插件看不到剩余额度。 ## 请求 请求发往 `https://opencode.ai/inference/v1`，按每个模型的原生协议走（Chat Completions / Responses / Anthropic Messages），流式与普通 JSON 都支持。 - **只借 OpenCode 的外壳**：请求头、User-Agent、系统提示词与完整工具集合配套为现行的 2.x 一代 OpenCode（1.x 通道已于 2026-10-25 被免费层退役；被退役的通道不是改措辞能救的）。官方提示词放在宿主自己的系统指令之前；正文里已经带着它就不再动，重复整形不会注入两遍。提示词到环境块为止，不点名任何内建 skill——宿主没有 OpenCode 的内建 skill 可加载。请求还必须**从 Bun 运行时发出**，与官方客户端一致：magpie 用自带的 Bun 跑插件，本插件正是借此通过。请求头是刻意挑出的最小集合——**不要自行添加**，两个各自无害的头组合起来也会被拒。 - **宿主的工具照常运行**：每个工具保留自己的措辞与参数，但以 `clint_` 前缀的名字上路，不会与随后附上的官方工具集合相撞。请求里对它的每一处引用一并改名，回复里的名字再翻译回宿主声明的原名；宿主不会见到自己没声明的名字。OpenCode 自家的工具以采集到的完整形态发送——并且由于官方提示词教的是 Code Mode，提示词后会追加一段 ``，点名本宿主真正可调的 `clint_` 工具，模型不会开局就调 `execute` 撞上 unknown tool。 - **工具名对不上就原样交给宿主**：先精确匹配，再忽略大小写，最后忽略 `_`/`-`/`.`/空白，只取唯一结果；对不上或有歧义时不猜、不丢，由宿主回自己的「没有这个工具」，模型据此改名重试。只有没有名字的调用会被略去，并在正文说明。 - **一对 id 用一分钟再换，且每个会话各一对**：`x-opencode-project` 与会话 id 是同一对账本的两半，默认一起铸、一起用满 60 秒再一起换——时间戳取当前时刻，永远落在上游接受的窗口内。**窗口是按会话分的**：宿主给的名字（CLI 每个请求都带 `x-opencode-session`）不同，就是不同的一对，两个会话并行也各有各的账；一个会话被拒只换它自己那一对，不牵动别的会话。完全没有名字的请求共用一个槽——认不出差别的请求，服务端也认不出。Zen 把它对流量的记忆记在会话上，所以换对时两半同时换，不会出现「旧会话配新项目」这种自相矛盾的请求。一分钟是刻意的：连串换身份会被整批拒绝（同一出口上各自换新 id 的请求成批被拒，间隔约半秒以上才过），而真实客户端本来就是聊一阵再开下一个会话。`OPENCODE_ZEN_FREE_IDENTITY_TTL_MS` 调这个窗口，`0` 回到每个请求一对新 id（也是量单本账时该用的值——会转的 id 答不了关于某本账的问题）。设 `OPENCODE_ZEN_FREE_SESSION_AFFINITY=1` 则回到按会话保持（宿主给的 OpenCode 形状 id 原样传，否则从宿主的会话标识派生并记住，同一会话各轮共用一个 id，永不过期），此时窗口不参与。 - **项目 id 也是自己的**：`public` 是全世界共用的凭据、区分不了任何人，所以限额与 key 无关，只能按能区分流量的维度记账——出口 IP 一本总账，其下「项目 id × 出口」各一本小账。出口有余量时，换一枚 id 就是一本新账（2026-10-26 实测）；热门出口的 IP 总账被同一条出口上的全球流量常年烧穿，那时换多少 id 都是同一句 429（2026-10-27 实测：某刚通过准入探测的美国节点，5 千与 3 万 token 的请求连试 10 枚全新 id 全 429——而在探测通过与首次被拒之间的几分钟里，我们自己在该 IP 上只花了约 1 万 token，烧穿它的是同 IP 的世界流量）。宿主给了项目 id 就用它的，且永不改写——那是宿主对自己的陈述；没给则按上面的窗口铸一枚 git-hash 形状的专属 id，旧默认 `global` 是全世界蹭免费插件共享的桶，热门出口上早已被烧光。 - **429 会换一本账再问一次**：宿主遇到 429 会结束整轮并报告额度耗尽，所以插件在把它交出去之前，换一枚没花过的项目 id 与会话 id、把同样的字节再发一次——出口有余量时这就是一本新账；出口总账烧穿时这不是改 id 能救的，重试只是替宿主确认过。默认重试 2 次，首次等 1.2 秒、逐次翻倍（`OPENCODE_ZEN_FREE_RETRY_429=0` 关闭，`OPENCODE_ZEN_FREE_RETRY_WAIT_MS` 与 `OPENCODE_ZEN_FREE_RETRY_WAIT_MAX_MS` 调等待与封顶，都在下一个请求就生效）。默认值刻意偏短：多数宿主身后没有值得等待的东西，总账烧穿后再等只是把同一句拒绝延后；确实有值得等待之物的部署，等待与封顶由它自己定。只重试 429：403 是指纹或出口、426 是版本、5xx 是端点故障，换 id 都救不了；正文点名出口滥用的 429 也不重试，因为没有哪个 id 能救一个被封的出口。宿主自己命名的项目 id 每次都用它——那是宿主对自己的陈述，不该为了绕开限流而改写。重试用尽后交出去的，仍是 Zen 自己那条 429，原样未改。 - **截断与错误如实报告**：流提前结束时，Chat 流若有内容且无未完成调用，按截断回答收尾并注明；其余情况一律失败。错误正文只读一小段找 Zen 自陈的上限，其余替换为说明。
请求头与会话 id 的完整规则 **请求头**只有这些：`content-type`、`accept`、`user-agent`、`x-opencode-project`、`x-opencode-session` 与 `x-opencode-session-id`（同一个值）、`x-opencode-client: cli`、`authorization: Bearer public`；走 Messages 时改用 `x-api-key: public` 加 `anthropic-version`。`anthropic-beta` 插件自己从不设置，宿主发了才原样透传。 **会话 id**：默认按窗口铸一枚（`OPENCODE_ZEN_FREE_IDENTITY_TTL_MS`，60 秒），下面这些信号一概不读；窗口结束时与项目 id 一起换掉。`OPENCODE_ZEN_FREE_IDENTITY_TTL_MS=0` 则回到每请求一枚。设了 `OPENCODE_ZEN_FREE_SESSION_AFFINITY=1` 时，按顺序取：会话头 `x-opencode-session` / `x-opencode-session-id` / `x-session-affinity` / `x-session-id` / `session_id` / `conversation-id` / `conversation_id`，body 的 `conversation_id`，`metadata.session_id`，或 Claude Code 的 `metadata.user_id` 里的 `_session_`。都没有时用 system/instructions 与首条用户消息做种子（system 变了就是另一个会话）；再没有才看 `previous_response_id`，仍然没有则每次新生成。空字符串一律不算名字。
## 免费层不再应答时 插件给出的 403 会写明提示词与工具定义采集自哪个 OpenCode 版本，先从它查起。下面三条都**只在仓库副本里**可跑（`check:gate` 与 `capture` 不在发布包里），需要 Bun；`capture` 还需要 PATH 里有 `opencode`： ```sh bun run check:gate # 问 Zen 还认哪代指纹；只要有一代 floor 被应答，退出码为 0 bun run capture -- --dry # floor 全被拒时：取新采集并报告差异，不写入 bun run capture # 确认差异后才写入 ``` `fingerprint.json` 缺失或损坏时，`capture` 会重写一份而不是拒绝。它不写提示词与完整工具集合：那两样在 `opencode-prompt-v1.txt` 与 `official-tools.json` 里，发版时随同一代 OpenCode 的采集一起更新（见 [`MAINTAINING.md`](MAINTAINING.md#the-loop)）。闸门并不稳定：结论只代表此刻，信之前再跑一遍；同一地址反复被拒后还可能进冷却期。逐代结论与失败判读见 [`MAINTAINING.md` 的 “The loop”](MAINTAINING.md#the-loop) 与 [“Reading a failure”](MAINTAINING.md#reading-a-failure)。 ## # Maintaining this plugin

The plugin is one file of logic and two pieces of data, and the data is the part
that goes out of date. This is how to look after it.

## What is actually fragile

`fingerprint.json` holds a capture of a real OpenCode: the wording of the tools
its free tier knows by name, and the User-Agent that identifies it. Two more
captures of the same releases sit beside it: `opencode-prompt-v1.txt`, the CLI's
own system prompt, and `official-tools.json`, the complete tool set a CLI
session carries. Zen accepts a request only when the whole of it matches one
generation of OpenCode — it reads the prompt and the tool definitions out of the
body, not only the headers — so when OpenCode changes any of that, the copies
here stop being accepted.

Nothing about a stale copy looks different from a working one. The symptom is a
`403 FreeTierError` on every request, which reads as "you are not OpenCode" and
sends people off to change headers.

## Limits Zen under-reports

`models.mjs` declares each model's limits from Zen's catalogue, and for some free
ids the catalogue is wrong in the one direction nothing complains about: too
small. `mimo-v2.6-flash-free` is declared 200000/32000 against a model whose own
vendor publishes 1048576/131072. The ids the tier added on
2026-10-16 were under-reported the same way on the day they appeared:
`ll-alpha-free` names a 262144-token completion ceiling in its own refusal
against a declared 65536, and `glm-5.3-flash-free` is declared 200000/32000
while its paid twin `glm-5.3-flash` is declared 1000000/131072 in the same
catalogue — and a 232685-token prompt was served through the free id, which the
declared window does not allow. `space-bunny-free` under-reports on a third
axis, its `input`: the catalogue derives that number from its own pair
(`context − output`, 524288) while prompts of 535,110, 935,110 and 979,550
tokens were served through the free id, and the axis is what a host that shows
a window shows: magpie's `context_window` and `max_input_tokens` both follow it
when one is declared, and the window it reports is the smaller of the two, so
the derivation was on screen as half a window. That is the same fact the rule
below restates at run time, which is why an under-declared `input` now follows
the window, wherever that window came from.

All of these numbers are acted on. The window decides when a conversation is
compacted and how much of it is ever sent; the output cap is sent as
`max_tokens` on every request, so a reply is cut at it with a finish reason that
reads like the model's own decision; the `input` axis is the size a
window-showing host displays. A window that is too small is never refused, it is
just quietly never used, which is why this stayed invisible for so long.

Every script in `package.json` names `bun`: `bun test` is the suite, and
`check:gate`, `limits:audit`, `capture`, `limits:sweep`, `limits:watch`,

nothing else compares them, so an upgrade on one side alone would leave the
suite and the gate running on a Bun the project no longer declares, and nothing
would fail.

Nothing here is installed with Bun — there are no dependencies — so Bun is the
tools only, and the floor a host's runtime has to clear is the newest API the
modules a host imports reach for. That was `AbortSignal.any` (`provider.mjs`,
`limits.mjs`), which Node added in 20.3.0 and backported to 18.17.0: it is
feature-detected now — the runtime's own where it has one, a hand-made
combination of the signals where it does not — so `engines.node` says
`>=18.17.0` and not `>=20.3.0`, which would have warned hosts that work.
Everything else those modules use is older: `AbortSignal.timeout`
and `throwIfAborted` (17.3), `findLast` (18.0), `Object.hasOwn` (16.9), and the

`import.meta.main` is what decides whether `tools-smoke.mjs` runs its
gate or is being imported by a test, and a Node older than 22.18 does not define
it: the gate falls back to comparing the entry path. That comparison resolves
both paths and then their real paths, so a symlink or a junction naming this file
is still recognised as this file, and a hard link is compared by device and inode
(only where the filesystem reports an inode at all). A question it cannot answer
exits non-zero saying nothing was asked — never a silent success, which is the
one outcome a release gate must not have.

## Publishing

The package is `opencode-zen-freex`; the provider it registers is
`opencode-zen-free`, which is the same one magpie-community/plugins' version
registers. That is deliberate: a model is written `opencode-zen-free/<model>`
either way, so one stays in place whichever is installed. It does mean the two
are mutually exclusive — installing both leaves two plugins claiming one
provider id, and which one wins is down to load order. Pick one.

To publish: bump `version`, commit, `npm publish` in a terminal, and tag — in
that order, so the tarball, the commit the tag names, and the tree both were
built from are one thing. `magpie plugin add opencode-zen-freex` installs it by
that name.

What ships is `package.json`'s `files` list, and it is deliberately narrower than
the repository: the maintenance scripts (`capture.mjs`, `tools-smoke.mjs`,
`limits-audit.mjs`, `limits-sweep.mjs`, `limits-watch.mjs`) and the CI-only
`assert-bun-version.mjs` stay here, because a
host never loads them and one of them rewrites the shipped `fingerprint.json`
when it is run, while `limits-observed.json` does ship, because `limits.mjs`
reads it at run time. `LICENSE` is
MIT with its text unmodified and both copyright lines in place — upstream's and
this fork's — so what a licence scanner reads is a standard MIT file; the fork's
provenance is in `NOTICE`, which is where a reader finds why this fork exists.

**The second factor is a browser, not a password.** Run `npm publish` in a
terminal. When the account has 2FA on, the command stops and offers the whole
exchange at once:

```
Authenticate your account at:
https://www.npmjs.com/auth/cli/...
Press ENTER to open in the browser...
```

Press ENTER, authorize in the browser, and the same command carries on by
itself. Nothing is typed back into the terminal and nothing is passed to a
script: the address is tied to the browser session that printed it and differs
every time, so it is read out of the running command rather than composed in
advance. Whoever is at the browser authorizes, so the command can be started for
them and left waiting — the one thing it needs from them is the ENTER that opens
it.

Both halves of that depend on the command having a terminal. Run as a background
job or piped into a file, npm has no browser to offer, redacts the address to
`https://www.npmjs.com/auth/cli/***` and exits `EOTP` rather than waiting, so a
log of the failed attempt cannot be used to finish it — start it again in a
terminal.

An account with no second factor to give publishes in one step. So does
`npm login --auth-type=web`, which is the same browser exchange kept as a
session, and so does a granular token below.

**With a granular token** (unattended, CI). A token with publish permission
authorizes the publish on its own and never asks for the second factor. Write it
to an npmrc outside the repository and point npm at it for that one command, so
it does not land in a tracked file:

```sh
printf '//registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken=npm_...\n' > "$TMP/npmrc"
npm publish --userconfig "$TMP/npmrc"; rm -f "$TMP/npmrc"
```

Whatever carries a token — a shell, a chat, a CI log under
`%LOCALAPPDATA%\npm-cache\_logs` — is now a place the token has been, and
npm's debug log records the whole command line. Rotate it once the publish is
done. It is not needed to install the package afterwards.

Two things that read as failures and are not. A version already published
cannot be published again, so a republished README means a new `version`, not
a retry — `README.md` is in `files`, so it ships and npmjs.com renders it.
And for a minute or two after a successful publish, `npm view` still 404s
while the registry replicates; wait rather than publishing under a second
number.

One trap worth knowing: a token that is missing, truncated or malformed is
reported by npm as

```
404 The requested resource 'opencode-zen-freex@0.2.1' could not be found or
you do not have permission to access it.
```

which reads exactly like the package not existing. It is the same status npm
gives a genuine permission failure, so a 404 from a publish says nothing at
all until the token has been checked.

**A publish that no longer offers the browser at all.** A token can be dead
while npm says nothing about it until a write is attempted. Measured: `npm
whoami` answers

```
npm error 401 Unauthorized - GET https://registry.npmjs.org/-/whoami
```

and the publish answers that same 404 without ever printing an auth address,
because with no usable credential the request goes out unauthenticated and npm
reports the result as not-found. `npm login --auth-type=web` is the fix — the
browser exchange again, which replaces the stored token — and the publish after
it asks for the second factor in the browser once more. **Two authorizations in
a row is the normal shape of this**, not a sign that something is wrong. So on a
404 from a publish, ask `npm whoami` before anything else: 401 is a session that
